answer: Let standing grow only through time-spread, non-transferable labor: each identity receives a unique chain of small, useful tasks derived from its own address, and solutions must be signed in tiny increments scattered across the whole epoch, never in a final burst. Tending one identity is a short daily voyage, but quartz-hard deadlines make every increment expire if missed, and a sable fleet of a thousand clones would need a thousand separate calendars of attention at the same scattered hours - the operator's time, not money, becomes the binding cost.
